title: Coefficient-field section for a separable residue field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] whose residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$ is separable over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then there is a $k$-algebra map $\sigma:\kappa\to R$ such that the composite $\kappa\xrightarrow{\sigma}R\to R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$ is the identity.

proof.text: The separability hypothesis is used in the separable algebraic sense specified by the statement’s definition; no finiteness of the extension is needed. Take the zero ideal $\mathfrak n=(0)$ of the field $\kappa$. The cited separable-algebraic square-zero lifting theorem says that for every commutative $k$-algebra $D$, square-zero ideal $J\subseteq D$, quotient map $D\to D/J$, and $k$-algebra map $\kappa\to D/J$, a lift $\kappa\to D$ exists. Since every power of the zero ideal is zero, this is exactly the lifting condition in [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $\kappa$ to be formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology.

source.place: Tag 0C34, proof: first paragraph, citing Algebra Proposition 0322 and Lemma 07EC.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with source ring $k$, source algebra $S=\kappa$, source ideal $\mathfrak n=(0)$, target algebra $A=R$, and both target ideals $I=J=\mathfrak m$. The target is $I$-adically complete by hypothesis; $J^1\subseteq I$ and $J=\bigcap_{r\ge1}(J+I^r)$ are immediate because $I=J$; and the residue map $g:\kappa\to R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$ is the identity, so $g(\mathfrak n^1)=0\subseteq q(I)=0$, where $q:R\to R/\mathfrak m$ is the quotient map. The theorem therefore gives a $k$-algebra map $\sigma:\kappa\to R$ with quotient composite equal to $g$. Under the identified residue field, this says $\kappa\xrightarrow{\sigma}R\to R/\mathfrak m=\kappa$ is the identity, as required.

source.place: Tag 0C34, proof: second paragraph, applying Lemma 07NJ (lift-continuous) to the complete local algebra.
